about.en:
The World Scholar's Cup is an international academic tournament for school students in teams of three. Every round covers the same interdisciplinary annual theme and has four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz), plus a talent show and social events.

Regional rounds are open to any team that registers, wherever its members live, so students can travel to a nearby round. Junior (roughly ages 10-14) and Senior (roughly 14-18) divisions compete separately, and strong results at a regional round earn an invitation to a Global Round and then the Tournament of Champions at Yale.

The Dilijan Round takes place on 23-24 November 2026 at UWC Dilijan, a residential international school in the forested hills of northern Armenia, about three hours by road from Tbilisi.

en: Hosted at UWC Dilijan, a 3-hour drive from Tbilisi
Debate, collaborative writing, quiz and individual test in English
Qualifying path to a Global Round and the Tournament of Champions at Yale

Travel to the host city for the two-day round.

The programme targets adults aged 18+, mainly at upper-elementary to intermediate level. It suits university students of Russian, Eurasian or Caucasus studies who want immersion in a safe, Russian-speaking city with easy visa-free access for many nationalities.

about.en:
The International Zhautykov Olympiad (IZhO) is a long-running international olympiad in mathematics, physics and computer science for secondary-school students, organised by Kazakhstan's Daryn centre at the Republican Physics and Mathematics School (Fizmat) in Almaty. The 2026 edition (10-15 January) gathered over 700 students from about 15 countries, including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Türkiye. The 23rd edition is expected in January 2027.

Each team has up to 3 mathematics, 2 physics and 2 computer-science contestants plus leaders; problems can be solved in the student's own language. Up to four teams per foreign country may take part, and teams are registered through the ministry of education or the body responsible for national olympiad teams. Medals and team rankings are awarded, and the olympiad is a strong stepping stone towards IMO, IPhO and IOI selection.

en: Maths, physics and informatics team olympiad with 700+ students
Food and accommodation in Almaty covered by organisers
Georgia regularly sends teams

eligibility.en: Secondary-school students strong in maths, physics or informatics, selected by their country's national olympiad body. Foreign teams must be registered through the ministry of education or the organisation that manages national olympiad teams (in Georgia, ask your olympiad coordinator or the Ministry/National Assessment and Examinations Center).

en: Do well in your national olympiad in maths, physics or informatics.
Ask your national olympiad coordinator or ministry whether your country will send an IZhO 2027 team.
The ministry pre-registers the team (2026 pattern: by mid-November) and confirms the full team (by mid-December).
Travel to Almaty in January with your team leader.

costs.en: Participation fee charged per participant and leader (USD 100 in recent invitations); organisers cover food and accommodation in Almaty; travel is paid by the sending country or school.

score_reason: Top regional olympiad, accommodation covered, Georgia participates; via national selection

Schools register delegations, and individual applications are also accepted. It is one of the most respected school MUNs in the region and a natural step for students from the Caucasus who want THIMUN-standard experience.

This competition is open to teams studying in Türkiye and abroad, so students from the Caucasus, Central Asia and elsewhere can enter.

Teams take a jet engine design through conceptual and critical design reviews with Q&A sessions held by the organisers, and the best designs are awarded at the festival.

In the 2026 cycle applications closed on 15 March 2026; the 2027 specification and calendar will be published on the competition page, and applications are made online through the TEKNOFEST portal. Finalists receive official digital certificates from the Ministry of Industry and Technology, training and Q&A sessions, technical tours, internship opportunities and, at university level, access to the TEKNOFEST Startup Program. 2026 first prize: TRY 200,000.
